{{Quote|The more you tighten your grip, Tarkin, the more star systems will slip through your fingers.|Leia Organa|<ref name="A New Hope" />|audio=LeiaSlipThroughYourFingers.flac}}
'''Wilhuff Tarkin''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] politician and military officer who was one of the most powerful [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moffs]] in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Tarkin was a leading figure in the shaping of Imperial doctrines and was the driving force behind the creation of its key embodiment, the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]].

Born on [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]] to the powerful and militaristic Human [[Tarkin family/Legends|Tarkin family]], the ambitious Tarkin began his career by serving in the [[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|Republic Outland Regions Security Force]]. He then retired and entered [[Politics/Legends|politics]], becoming [[Lieutenant governor/Legends|lieutenant governor]] and later full Governor of Eriadu and the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]], before returning to the [[Republic Military/Legends|military]] in order to serve [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] as an agent of the secret [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord's]] [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] movement. It was in that time that Tarkin learned of his friend [[Raith Sienar/Legends|Raith Sienar's]] designs for the [[Expeditionary Battle Planetoid]] and, convinced of the potential of the design, presented Palpatine with the plans for what would become the Death Star.

Tarkin gained increasing stature as a vocal supporter of Palpatine and received notice as the Seswenna sector's [[Governor/Legends|governor]] throughout the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. At one point, he served as a [[Captain/Legends|captain]] under [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Even Piell/Legends|Even Piell]], where he and his crew were held in the [[Citadel/Legends|Citadel]], a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Prison/Legends|prison]], and [[Battle of Lola Sayu/Legends|escaped]] with the help of a strike team of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]]. Later on, he had been promoted to [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]]. He was present during the capture of [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] after the [[Battle of Xagobah (Clone Wars)|Battle of Xagobah]]. In the last days of the Clone Wars, Palpatine appointed Tarkin as the first [[Moff/Legends|Moff]], and when the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Declaration of a New Order|became]] the Galactic Empire, the new [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine gave him oversight of the construction of the Death Star. Tarkin soon formulated the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]], which helped solidify his reputation as the greatest architect of the Empire save Palpatine. The Tarkin Doctrine called for rule of the galaxy through fear of overwhelming force, and recommended the creation of [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]] such as the Death Star to create terror of Imperial reprisal that would stifle any thoughts of rebellion. Delighted, Palpatine made Tarkin the first Grand Moff, giving him control of nearly the entire [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].

As Grand Moff, Tarkin ruled with the same unyielding ruthlessness he had helped enshrine in Imperial doctrine, often cooperating with [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. As the long-delayed construction of the Death Star stalled, Tarkin created the secret [[Maw Installation]] to refine the design, placing it under the control of his mistress and protégée, Admiral [[Natasi Daala]]. With the aid of the Maw Installation's [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]], the Death Star was finally made operational in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]. Confident he could destroy the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|opposing]] the Empire, Tarkin began his campaign of fear by [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destroying]] [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], a hotbed of Rebel sentiment. Tarkin then allowed prominent Rebel [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], captive aboard the Death Star, to [[Rescue of Princess Leia/Legends|escape]] and lead the Death Star to the secret Rebel [[Great Temple/Legends|base]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. There, seconds away from annihilating the Rebel headquarters, Tarkin [[Death/Legends|died]] when [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|destroyed]] the Death Star, a victim of his own belief in the Death Star's invincibility.

==Biography==
===Ambition and ascent===
{{Quote|The old ways are dying. We have to adapt. I have adapted.|Wilhuff Tarkin, to Raith Sienar|<ref name="Rogue Planet" />}}
Wilhuff Tarkin was born into the [[Tarkin family/Legends|Tarkin family]], an old, wealthy and powerful clan that had originally been granted the world of [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]] and still remained dominant in the politics and business of Eriadu and the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]], as well as carrying strong influence in galactic politics.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /><ref name="Rebellion Era Sourcebook">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref> He and his younger brother, [[Gideon Tarkin]], grew up in a family steeped in tradition, prestige, and accomplishment in politics, science, the arts, and the military.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Rebellion Era Sourcebook" /> Tarkin's older cousin was [[Ranulph Tarkin/Legends|Ranulph Tarkin]], [[Senator/Legends|senator]] for the Seswenna sector and a leading [[Militarists/Legends|Militarist]]&mdash;and after his [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]] death in the [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]], a war hero.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /><ref name="The Stark Hyperspace War">''[[Star Wars: The Stark Hyperspace War]]''</ref> Though Tarkin took pride in his family's history of service to the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and accomplishments on Eriadu, he resented the lack of respect his [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]-based clan received in comparison to the aristocratic families of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], fueling in him a burning ambition to excel.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" />

[[File:TarkinTFUCG.jpg|thumb|right|180px|A young Wilhuff Tarkin]]
As a young man, Tarkin enrolled in a military academy, in accordance with the Tarkin family's strong military tradition.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Rogue Planet" /> Driven to live up to every aspect of the family legacy, young Wilhuff Tarkin cultivated expertise in multiple fields, establishing a reputation as an intellectual prodigy with a well-rounded mind. He displayed great aptitude as a tactician in the course of his schooling, drafted starship designs that inspired the design of [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|interdictor craft]], broke new ground in [[xenobiology]] theory, and demonstrated great talent as a poet and philosopher.<ref name="Rebellion Era Sourcebook" /> A keen analyst of the political situation, Tarkin perceived the Galactic Republic to be a decaying institution, and envisioned a new future for the galaxy.<ref name="Annual 2008">''[[Star Wars Annual 2008]]''</ref> His vision was a militant one, authoritarian and [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentric]], and he possessed a driving ambition to rise to the ranks of power, where he could affect change.<ref name="Rogue Planet" /><ref name="Cloak of Deception">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref>

After graduation, he and his brother Gideon joined the [[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|Republic Outland Regions Security Force]], a military policing force that kept the [[Outland Regions]], a Rim area that included Eriadu, safe from piracy.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Cloak of Deception" /> Tarkin was a fast riser who achieved the rank of [[Commander/Legends|commander]], and during the course of his service visited [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], capital of the galaxy, several times.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> There, around [[39 BBY/Legends|39 BBY]], he befriended [[Raith Sienar/Legends|Raith Sienar]], heir to the [[Republic Sienar Systems/Legends|Republic Sienar Systems]] shipbuilding concern and an accomplished engineer who was near Tarkin's age.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Rogue Planet" />

[[File:RaithSienarHS-NEGTC.png|thumb|left|180px|Tarkin befriended Raith Sienar.]]
Still a young man, Commander Tarkin retired from the military in order to seek a political career on Eriadu.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> With the aid of his family's political heft and numerous connections, Tarkin was elected the [[Lieutenant governor/Legends|lieutenant governor]] of Eriadu and the Seswenna sector by [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], dwelling in an elegant [[Wilhuff Tarkin's mansion|mansion]] on [[Eriadu City/Legends|Eriadu City's]] bay.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Cloak of Deception" /> A rising politician, Tarkin was acquainted with Senator [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], himself an influential member of the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]&mdash;and secretly the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] Darth Sidious, in which guise he appealed to Tarkin's speciesism and convinced Tarkin to serve his agenda.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> Tarkin gained a measure of notoriety in galactic political circles for his militant views, while on Eriadu he was known as a foe of the Eriaduan branch of [[House Valorum/Legends|House Valorum]].<ref name="Cloak of Deception" /> Though he was subordinate to the sector governor, Tarkin was an active force in Eriaduan life, taking a strong hand in political, military, and economic affairs.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" />

When, in 33 BBY, Palpatine saw profit in manipulating the competition between [[Lommite Limited]] and [[InterGalactic Ore]], two rival [[Lommite/Legends|lommite]] companies from nearby [[Dorvalla/Legends|Dorvalla]], Lieutenant Governor Tarkin arranged a contract with each company to deliver lommite to Eriadu on short notice, casting it as a competition for a long-term supply contract that could provide one company with dominance over the other. Tarkin set up a ceremony on an orbital habitat, scheduled for the arrival of the contesting shipments, featuring himself, the heads of each company, and the executive officers of [[Eriadu Manufacturing]] and [[Valorum Shipping and Transport]], Eriadu's two main lommite consumers. The two convoys, however, were sabotaged, and collided upon exiting hyperspace early. The disaster forced Lommite Limited and InterGalactic Ore into a merger as [[Dorvalla Mining]], which granted its shipping rights to the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]]. The power of [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] Trade Federation [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], a pawn of Palpatine, increased as the result of his involvement in the deal.<ref name="Saboteur">"[[Darth Maul: Saboteur]]"</ref>

When [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] suggested the taxation of the former free trade zone of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid]] and Outer Rim as part of a deal allowing the Trade Federation to increase its defense allotments to respond to attacks by pirates and the [[Nebula Front/Legends|Nebula Front]] terrorist movement, Palpatine suggested a conference be held on Eriadu to iron out the issue. Tarkin hosted the Supreme Chancellor at his seaside [[Wilhuff Tarkin's mansion|mansion]], which was overrun with security personnel well before he was able to personally receive Valorum.<ref name="Cloak of Deception" /> Tarkin was in fact complicit in Darth Sidious's scheme to murder most of the [[Trade Federation Directorate]]<ref name="Grand Moff Tarkin">{{InsiderCite|113|Dark Forces: The Villains of Star Wars|Dark Forces: The Villains of ''Star Wars''}}</ref> at the summit, which would place the Neimoidian faction serving Sidious at the head of the Trade Federation.<ref name="Cloak of Deception" />

As Tarkin was about to leave with Valorum for the opening of the [[Eriadu Trade Summit]], the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] assigned to protect Valorum informed the Supreme Chancellor of evidence of a Nebula Front conspiracy to assassinate him. Though Valorum was reluctant to show fear by increasing his protection, Tarkin convinced him to take some precautions. Tarkin authorized Eriaduan security forces to take any necessary measures to ensure the Supreme Chancellor's safety, instructing them to put efficacy over legality. Valorum, though, was not the true target, and the Nebula Front was able to carry out the assassination of almost the entire Trade Federation Directorate as Tarkin watched in [[Seswenna Hall/Legends|Seswenna Hall]]. Valorum assigned the [[Judicial Department/Legends|Judicial Department]] to investigate the incident, but, serving Palpatine's interests, Tarkin stonewalled the effort by claiming Eriaduan jurisdiction, then ensuring that the investigation stalled until most evidence had been lost.<ref name="Cloak of Deception" />

Valorum was weakened in the wake of the scandal, and in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], he was ousted from the Supreme Chancellorship and replaced with Palpatine.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> Tarkin had previously attempted to curry favor with multiple factions, but he saw a sea change in the political situation and moved to ally himself more closely with Palpatine's administration.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Rogue Planet" /> He became connected to the secretive but emergent [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] movement quietly building in the government, which agreed with Tarkin's authoritarian, militaristic, and Humanocentric beliefs. Tarkin left office, and Supreme Chancellor Palpatine reactivated Tarkin's commission and moved him to Coruscant, where he became a valuable agent of the New Order.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> Tarkin kept a small but prestigiously located apartment high in [[Prime Senate Spire]]. Tarkin's service earned him the right to wear [[robes of senatorial favor]], a distinguishing honor that signified exceptional service to the Galactic Senate.<ref name="Rogue Planet" />

One of Tarkin's assignments was to monitor the Jedi and work to prevent any increases in their power. In the course of his surveillance, he learned that young Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] had a habit of repairing droids, and placed a broken droid, programmed to spy, so that Skywalker would come across it.<ref name="Rogue Planet" /> The young Jedi restored the droid to functionality and allowed it to roam the halls of the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]], which gave Tarkin the ability to eavesdrop on many sensitive private conversations, including [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] meetings.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> Tarkin was also secretly involved with a Trade Federation-aligned association of assassins that targeted the Jedi.<ref name="Rogue Planet" />

===Zonama Sekot===
{{Quote|I hope you understand what could be at stake here. At the moment we are merely useful lackeys. We are below the level of awareness of those who will command the galaxy. If this planet and its ships are as useful as they appear to be, we will be richly rewarded. We will be noticed. Some already share my belief that this could be very big.|Wilhuff Tarkin, to Raith Sienar|<ref name="Rogue Planet" />}}
In [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]], Tarkin attended a secret meeting in which he learned that Palpatine had, after three years, forced a resolution to the fallout from the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|attack]] the Trade Federation had staged on Naboo over the taxation of the trade routes. The Trade Federation security forces were to be disbanded and disarmed, their assets turned over to the Republic. The main focus for Tarkin, however, was a mission to seek out [[Zonama Sekot/Legends|Zonama Sekot]]&mdash;a mysterious and remote planet, considered half legend but rumored to produce extraordinary living starships&mdash;and obtain one of its starships, or even control over the planet.<ref name="Rogue Planet" />

[[File:Tarkin-SWE.png|thumb|right|180px|Tarkin during the last days of the Galactic Republic]]
He came afterward to see his old friend Raith Sienar, who had by that time ascended to control of the Sienar business empire, and whom Tarkin knew to secretly have a Sekotan ship. Tarkin explained to Sienar the nature of Zonama Sekot and asked for his expertise, but did not bring up the ship when Sienar pretended unfamiliarity with the planet. During the meeting, Tarkin observed and was fascinated by Sienar's designs for an [[Expeditionary Battle Planetoid]], a massive [[Space station/Legends|space station]] designed to control star systems, which featured a giant [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] powered directly by the station's core.<ref name="Rogue Planet" /> Tarkin saw tremendous potential in the concept, especially if the defensively potent design's weapon was upgraded to provide sufficient power to ruin a world; fear of such a weapon's visitation, he believed, would solve the ancient problem of how to keep order in a galaxy too large for any fleet to patrol effectively and deny support to guerrilla movements.<ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

Soon afterward, Tarkin was forced to put his plan into action abruptly when he found that the Jedi were sending a mission of their own to Zonama Sekot. Tarkin, using a tracker he had planted on Sienar, followed the engineer into his secret hall of engineering failures, bringing Ke Daiv as a bodyguard, and demanded that Sienar provide access to the tracking beacon he had built into the ship ''[[Star Sea Flower]]''&mdash;the transport used by the Jedi expedition&mdash;during a refitting. He then asked Sienar to command the venture to Zonama Sekot, an offer the other man accepted. He briefed Sienar on the expedition, which was to consist of decommissioned Trade Federation ships and their crews, which had not yet been turned over to the Republic, as well as Daiv, who would report back to Tarkin. They then had to wait for the Jedi ship to reach Zonama Sekot, allowing them to learn the planet's location through the tracking device. During that time, Tarkin imposed on Sienar to show him the Sekotan ship that Sienar owned, though there was little to be learned from the dead craft. Once the ''Star Sea Flower'' emerged from hyperspace, Tarkin rushed Sienar to his task force and sent him off. Observing his lackluster forces, Sienar accused Tarkin of rigging the situation so that Sienar would fail, but the commander denied that allegation.<ref name="Rogue Planet" />

As Sienar's expedition drew on with no report, Tarkin sent Sienar a message asking for an update. Sienar, seeking to bring Tarkin running, sent a reply that falsely stated that Daiv had failed in an attempt to assassinate him and had been sent on a suicide mission, and that Sienar had found something magnificent and required no assistance. Having played on his contacts in the Senate for greater support, Tarkin rushed a task force of Republic vessels, stronger than the one he had assigned Sienar, to Zonama Sekot in order to take control of the situation, and activated the hidden programming he had buried in Sienar's [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|droid starfighters]] to impel them into an attack on the planet&mdash;the conflict justifying Tarkin in taking a more militaristic approach when he arrived. Sienar was able to disable most of the droids before they launched, but Tarkin had [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Kett (Galactic Republic)|Kett]], captain of Sienar's flagship ''[[Admiral Korvin]]'', place Sienar under arrest. Sienar would not comply with Tarkin's request that he be given access to the new programming with which he knew Sienar had equipped his droid complement, so Tarkin transferred to the ''Admiral Korvin'' and escorted his former friend to his own flagship, ''[[Rim Merchant Einem]]''.<ref name="Rogue Planet" />

Tarkin launched the invasion with his own forces, justifying it as a police action involving a starship chase he observed in the atmosphere. He deployed [[sky mine]]s and droid starfighters, giving the planet's inhabitants no warning. He was surprised when the world deployed greater defenses than he had expected, launching waves of ships that brought down many of Tarkin's starfighters. Tarkin located one large Sekotan ship that had set down on its own, and landed with his forces to capture it. He recognized the pilot as Anakin Skywalker, a member of the Jedi expedition to the planet, and took him and the ship aboard the [[sky-mine delivery ship]] he had used as a landing craft. Tarkin questioned the boy about the ship, nearly provoking him into attacking Tarkin with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. The ''Star Sea Flower'' began boarding the ship in a rescue effort led by Skywalker's [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], and Tarkin rushed from the hangar bay. The Jedi escaped in the ''[[Jabitha]]'', their Sekotan ship, while Tarkin had to abandon the minelayer, which the Jedi had rigged with explosives, in an escape pod that he shared with Sienar.<ref name="Rogue Planet" />

Recovered by the ''Rim Merchant Einem'', Tarkin launched a renewed assault on the planet. To his shock, Zonama Sekot engaged massive engines and the entire planet jumped to hyperspace. The effect of its jump hurled Tarkin's fleet into chaos, while the Jedi escaped. Tarkin managed to limp his fleet home and, called before Palpatine, presented him with Sienar's plans for the Expeditionary Battle Planetoid, taking sole credit for the design. Sienar, uneasy with the design, did not dispute him, and the design allowed Tarkin to redeem his failure to secure Zonama Sekot for Palpatine, who was interested in the concept.<ref name="Rogue Planet" /> Palpatine began work on bringing the project to fruition himself, having the plans refined by engineer [[Bevel Lemelisk]] in collaboration with [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] engineers, while Republic researchers worked on component systems.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> Having been cut out of the process, Tarkin believed that Palpatine had ultimately abandoned the plans.<ref name="Death Star">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref>

===The Clone Wars begin===
{{Quote|You lack faith in the Jedi.''"<br />"''I find their tactics ineffective. The Jedi Code prevents them from going far enough to achieve victory, to do whatever it takes to win, the very reason why peacekeepers should not be leading a war. Have I&hellip;offended you?''"<br />"''No. I've also found that we sometimes fall short of victory because of our methods.''"<br />"''Well, I see we agree on something.|Anakin Skywalker and Tarkin|<ref name="Counterattack">{{TCW|Counterattack}}</ref>}}
Tarkin was known for his support of Palpatine and intellectual argumentation in favor of the Chancellor's moves to consolidate power, and frequently advocated Palpatine's policies before the Galactic Senate, a venue in which he had great success.<ref name="NewsNets 3">{{JournalCite|3|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref><ref name="Galaxy Guide 1">''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]''</ref><ref name="The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Tarkin had many friends within the Senate, as well as in the business realm, contacts that allowed him to further rise in influence.<ref name="Annual 2008" /> By [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Tarkin was serving as the governor of Eriadu and the Seswenna sector.<ref name="Official Starships & Vehicles 9" /> His brother, [[Brigadier]] Gideon Tarkin, served as his [[Minister of Security]], while relative [[Shayla Paige-Tarkin]] represented the sector in the Senate. Under Tarkin, the sector remained loyal to the Republic, even as the region became a hotspot of activity for the growing [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist movement]] and the neighboring [[Sluis sector/Legends|Sluis sector]] seceded.<ref name="IBC Denies Arming Separatists">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|55|business/1359_1.html|IBC Denies Arming Separatists}}</ref><ref name="Sluis Sector Secedes">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|49|news/13328_4.html|Sluis Sector Secedes; Seswenna Restates Loyalty}}</ref>

In 22 BBY, the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] broke out between the Republic and the secessionist government, the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> Eriadu was a major Republic stronghold during the war, a significant forward position surrounded by heavily armed Separatist sectors&mdash;and it was under Tarkin's command.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /><ref name="Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> Gideon Tarkin commanded the Republic's fleet in the area. Eriadu and [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]] were the region's key fortresses, but in the second year of the war, Sullust defected to the Confederacy. Tarkin's brother commanded a major offensive directed against Sullust, losing the [[Battle of Sullust (Republic traitor)|Battle of Sullust]] but seizing much of the Sluis sector from the Separatists.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> While Gideon Tarkin was holding off the enemy, Governor Wilhuff Tarkin, too, made a name for himself in the Clone Wars. Not all was fighting, as he engaged in multiple negotiations with the Separatists, and was aided in many of them by Jedi Master [[Luminara Unduli/Legends|Luminara Unduli]].<ref name="Pursuit">''[[Boba Fett: Pursuit]]''</ref>

[[File:TarkinRex-TC.png|thumb|left|200px|Captain Tarkin inside the Citadel prison]]
Even with his position as Governor during the Clone Wars, Tarkin was able to be recommissioned into the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] as an [[Republic officer/Legends|officer]]. While serving as captain of a [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class]] [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] under the command of [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Even Piell/Legends|Even Piell]], Tarkin and Piell undertook a mission to find the [[Nexus Route/Legends|Nexus Route]], a strategically valuable [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace route]] which would lead into both the heart of the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems. During the mission, however, they were [[Capture of Even Piell/Legends|ambushed and attacked]] by Separatist forces. Before they were boarded, Piell and Tarkin each memorized half of the information regarding the Nexus Route before erasing it from the ship's computer files. After being forced to surrender, Tarkin and Piell, along with other officers were taken as prisoners to the [[Citadel/Legends|Citadel]], a Separatist [[Prison/Legends|prison]] on [[Lola Sayu/Legends|Lola Sayu]]. Once Piell was freed from captivity by a rescue team led by the Generals Obi-Wan Kenobi, Anakin Skywalker and [[Jedi Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]], Piell informed his liberators that Captain Tarkin possessed the other half of the Nexus Route coordinates. Making their way towards the prison cell holding the Republic officers, the Jedi succeeded in freeing Tarkin and the [[Clone navigation officer/Legends|clone officers]].<ref name="The Citadel" />

Although initially surprised to see his Jedi superior officer again, and elated to be redeemed from capture, Tarkin quickly became pessimistic about the overall situation since they were still in the heart of enemy territory. After taking a moment to consider General Kenobi's escape plan, Tarkin interjected with an idea of his own&mdash;to keep the group, small as it already was, together in order to improve their chances of both protecting the valuable information and escaping from the Citadel. Although he tried to convince the group that greater strength could be found in greater numbers as opposed to a divided group, General Piell concurred with General Kenobi and told Tarkin to accompany General Skywalker's group. Tarkin, slightly annoyed that his idea was flat-out rejected, nonetheless did as commanded and followed Skywalker, Tano and a group of clones into the old tunnels beneath the Citadel.<ref name="The Citadel" />

[[File:TarkinSnipesAtAnakin-TC.png|thumb|right|250px|Tarkin speaks his mind to Anakin Skywalker, shortly after being rescued by the Jedi.]]
After Skywalker commented on how everything was proceeding according to Kenobi's plan thus far, Tarkin once again gave voice to his pragmatism by asking what would happen if things stopped going according to plan. Although slightly annoyed by the outspoken and opinionated Republic officer, Skywalker insisted that Tarkin trust him because of the fact that Jedi can be quite good at improvising whenever plans failed. When Tarkin claimed that he only trusted those who took action, Skywalker retorted that he only trusted those who understood the concept of ''gratitude'', reminding Tarkin that he would still be a helpless prisoner if it weren't for the efforts of the Jedi.<ref name="The Citadel" />

While Skywalker's Padawan, Tano, took point, Tarkin lacked faith in the young Padawan's ability to lead the group. [[Clone Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Rex/Legends|Rex]] tried to assure Tarkin that his experience with Ahsoka enabled him to trust in her abilities, but Tarkin was hardly convinced and dismissed the clone's assessment of Tano with silence. As the group continued to make their way to the rendezvous via the old tunnel system, Tarkin became increasingly impressed with the layout of the Citadel and its virtually impregnable status&mdash;much to the surprise of Tano. Tarkin merely chided her for being short-sighted and explained that their entire ordeal only proves the Citadel's strategic worth, thus causing him to lament on how the fortress was seized by the Separatists rather than the Republic. Skywalker agreed with Tarkin's point of view of the matter.<ref name="Counterattack" />

Meanwhile, Tarkin admitted that while Skywalker had managed to earn his trust, the rest of the Jedi Order fell short in that regard. Not only did Tarkin find their tactics ineffective, he also felt that the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]] was far too restricting in the sense that it prevented its adherents from escalating their efforts to win the war. Rather than feeling offended, Skywalker found Tarkin's argument enlightening and agreed that the Jedi were not doing enough to defeat the Separatists, thus providing a sense of common ground between the two.<ref name="Counterattack" />

By the time they reached the shuttle's location, the Separatist garrison had already caught on to them and proceeded to cut off their only means of escape. Tarkin argued that a forward charge was necessary in order to reach the shuttle and use its weaponry to annihilate their attackers. Before anything could be done, however, the shuttle was destroyed and the group was forced to retreat as they became quickly overwhelmed by the enemy's numbers.<ref name="Counterattack" />

Once they were provided with a set of coordinates to the location where they would be rescued, Tarkin wondered what the group's contingency plan would be if the Jedi failed to rescue them, much to the annoyance of General Piell. When Skywalker tried to caution Tarkin against arguing with a Jedi superior officer, Tarkin was unfazed and declared that he stood by his principles without hesitation or compromise. He also did not care much for his standoff with General Piell, feeling confident that his career was perfectly secured as he had fallen into the favor of Supreme Chancellor Palpatine. Skywalker responded by mentioning his own friendship with the Chancellor, thus further impressing Tarkin and allowing the two to develop a greater sense of mutual respect.<ref name="Citadel Rescue">{{TCW|Citadel Rescue}}</ref>

[[File:AhsokaTarkin-CR.png|thumb|left|250px|Tano and Tarkin on Coruscant, following the success of the rescue operation.]]
After another short skirmish with the Separatists, Tarkin and most of the group emerged unscathed&mdash;but General Piell fell in battle. Tarkin was visibly dismayed to learn that prior to the general's death, Piell shared his half of the intel with Tano. When the group made it to their destination, they found their position assaulted by the Separatists led by the Citadel's sadistic caretaker [[Osi Sobeck/Legends|Osi Sobeck]]. As the Jedi and clones held their ground, Sobeck was momentarily disarmed and at the mercy of Tarkin. Seizing the opportunity, Tarkin confidently approached Sobeck and attempted to execute him, but failed as Sobeck swiftly retaliated and nearly killed Tarkin. However, Tarkin was rescued just in time by Tano, who used her lightsaber to stab Sobeck in the back. At that moment, the Jedi rescue team arrived and was able to shuttle the group off of the planet and back to the safety of Coruscant.<ref name="Citadel Rescue" />

After arriving at the Jedi Temple, Tarkin and the group were welcomed back by Jedi Masters [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] and [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]]. But when Yoda moved to debrief Tarkin and Tano on the information regarding the Nexus Route, Tarkin insisted that his orders strictly forbade him from sharing the information with anyone other than Chancellor Palpatine. Likewise, Tano promised Piell that she would only share her half of the information with the Jedi Council, thus creating an obvious stalemate. Yoda assured everyone that he would speak with the Chancellor in order to reach a reasonable compromise. Before departing to report to the Chancellor, Tarkin congratulated Skywalker and the two shook hands, thus solidifying their new-found friendship. Aside from voicing his wish that more Jedi were like Skywalker, he suggested that he would inform the Chancellor of Skywalker's valor on Lola Sayu. As Tarkin disembarked to give his report to the Chancellor at the [[Republic Executive Building/Legends|Republic Executive Building]], Kenobi confessed his disapproval of the new friendship between his former Padawan and Tarkin. Skywalker remained resolute in his defense of the Republic captain, however, and believed that Tarkin's hardline stance was exactly what the Republic needed, especially in a time of crisis when the Separatists threatened to split the galaxy in half.<ref name="Citadel Rescue" />

===New allies and enemies===
{{Quote|Dire circumstances demand that I must be blunt: I fear the Jedi Order will lose this war if they are allowed to continue in their role as the leadership of the Grand Army of the Republic. These recent weeks have piled debacle upon debacle upon us, and I cannot sit in silence and still call myself a patriot. I have expressed concerns of this type to you in the past, and you've been generous enough to offer an attentive ear. I know your time is valuable, so this is not just a repetition of earlier misgivings.|Admiral Tarkin, in his letter to Chancellor Palpatine|<ref name="Reformation of Jedi military command">{{Facebook|username=StarWarsTheCloneWars|url=photo.php?fbid=494382640601035|name=''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''|date=2013-01-15|archivefile=File:Memo.jpg}}</ref>}}
Later in the war, Tarkin was promoted to [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] and was present at the [[Republic strategy conference/Legends|Republic strategy conference]] held in the [[Carida system/Legends|Carida system]] on the space station [[Valor (space station)/Legends|Valor]]. At the conference a [[Renown/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] that had been hijacked and loaded with explosive [[Rhydonium/Legends|rhydonium]] by the Separatists approached the station, and Tarkin attempted to contact the ship, but received no reply. He then scanned the ship and discovered it was loaded with the explosives. However, the Star Destroyer was destroyed by the astromech droid [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], saving the Republic personnel at the conference.<ref name="PONR">{{TCW|Point of No Return (The Clone Wars)}}</ref> Nonetheless, after being debriefed on the event, later known as the [[Carida Incident]], Tarkin, deeply disturbed at the event (which occurred during a military plan by the Jedi Order without apparent Military authorization to retrieve a Separatist decryption module, and utilized [[D-Squad/Legends|some droids]] and an [[Meebur Gascon/Legends|inexperienced tactical commander]]) and the very narrow aversion of a disaster, wrote a [[Reformation of Jedi military command|memorandum]] requesting for gradually phasing the Jedi out of military command of the Clone Wars if the Galactic Republic were going to win it, as he feared that as long as the Jedi Order stayed in command of the Grand Army of the Republic, the Republic would continue to suffer defeats at the hands of the Separatists and eventually lose the war.<ref name="Reformation of Jedi military command" />

[[File:TarkinProscecutor.png|thumb|right|230px|Tarkin accuses Ahsoka Tano of the bombing of the Jedi Temple at her trial.]]
Admiral Tarkin attended the [[Funeral of the Jedi Temple bombing victims/Legends|funeral]] for the victims of the [[Bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar/Legends|Bombing of the Jedi Temple Hangar]]. Afterwards, he informed Ahsoka Tano and Anakin Skywalker that the accused perpetrator of the bombing, [[Letta Turmond/Legends|Letta Turmond]], was being transferred from the Jedi Temple to military custody. Tano protested this method of handling the situation, but Tarkin explained that because Turmond was not a Jedi and clones had been killed in the bombing, the Republic military had jurisdiction. Skywalker scolded Tano for becoming angry, and after Tano had left, he lamented to Tarkin that his Padawan still had much to learn.

Later, Tarkin informed Tano that Turmond wished to speak with her and Tano consented. While Tano was with Turmond in her cell, Turmond was strangled with the Force, and Tano was arrested because it was assumed that she was Turmond's killer. Tarkin visited Tano in her cell and showed her the recording of the incident, which, without sound, made it seem as though Tano was reaching toward the floating Turmond to choke her, rather than help her. Tarkin ordered that no one be able to visit Tano, much to Skywalker's dismay, but Tano was soon able to [[Escape from the Republic military base/Legends|escape]] from the [[Republic military base|military base]] where she was being held.<ref name="TKWKTM">{{TCW|The Jedi Who Knew Too Much}}</ref>

Ahsoka Tano was soon recaptured, and Tarkin came before the Jedi Council on behalf of the Senate to request that Tano be expelled from the Jedi Order so that she could be tried by a military tribunal. It was feared that a trial by the Jedi would seem biased. The Jedi Council obliged, and Tano was [[Trial of Ahsoka Tano/Legends|tried]] before a jury of senators, with Tarkin heading the prosecution and [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] heading the defense. Tarkin declared that he would prove Tano guilty of both the Temple bombing and the murder of her cohorts, and asked that the death penalty be used as punishment. Amidala argued that Tano was being framed, because if Tano was truly guilty, she would not have made the evidence against herself so obvious. Tarkin cast doubt on Tano's claims by mentioning that Tano had been seen with the Separatist war criminal [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]].

Eventually, the arguments concluded, and the jury reached a decision. As Supreme Chancellor Palpatine started to read the verdict, Anakin Skywalker and members of the [[Jedi Temple Guard/Legends|Jedi Temple Guard]] arrived in the courtroom with the Jedi [[Barriss Offee/Legends|Barriss Offee]]. Offee confessed to having committed the crimes of which Tano was accused, and the charges against Tano were dropped, though as a result of feeling betrayed and disillusioned, Tano refused to return to the Jedi.<ref name="TWJ">{{TCW|The Wrong Jedi}}</ref>

===Gaining authority===
{{Quote|This is a high-stakes game we're involved in. As you've noticed, I have some distance to cover in this new hierarchy. Eventually, I hope to be awarded a provincial governorship, and to control many star systems.|Wilhuff Tarkin, to Raith Sienar|<ref name="Rogue Planet" />}}
[[File:Threemoffs.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Tarkin, featured in a report on the new system of Moffs]]
During the course of the Clone Wars, Tarkin discovered the world of [[Omwat/Legends|Omwat]]. He recognized the native [[Omwati/Legends|Omwati]]; an enclave of the species existed on Coruscant, but their homeworld had lost contact with the galaxy since that colony had been established. Tarkin had been impressed with the mental ability of the Coruscanti Omwati, and decided that Omwat could prove a useful resource. He kept its location secret, hoping to have a future opportunity to exploit the intellect of the species.<ref name="Alien Anthology">''[[Alien Anthology]]''</ref>

In the closing months of the Clone Wars, Palpatine implemented the [[Sector Governance Decree/Legends|Sector Governance Decree]], which placed regional and planetary military governors in control of the Republic's systems.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> Admiral Tarkin, who had risen rapidly to prominence in Palpatine's government, was the first man appointed as a regional governor and given the ancient title of [[Moff/Legends|Moff]].<ref name="The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide" /><ref name="Dark Lord">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref><ref name="Republic HoloNet News">{{InsiderCite|84|Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241}}</ref> Tarkin was among twenty elite Moffs given control of a [[Sector Army/Legends|Sector Army]], one of the major divisions of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]], and a military territory, the [[Greater Seswenna/Legends|Greater Seswenna]], corresponding to the Sector Army's area of operations. These oversized territories, crossing normal sector boundaries, were referred to as [[Oversector/Legends|oversectors]].<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> Tarkin's appointment drew attention, and he was profiled in a [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] feature on the new system of Moffs.<ref name="Republic HoloNet News" /> Commanding a mixed force of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] and the Outland Regions Security Force in the [[Eighteenth Army]] to defend the besieged salient around Eriadu, the actions of Tarkin and his army were feted in Republic propaganda.<ref name="Warfare" />

When the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]] began and the Separatists were forced on to the defensive, Tarkin's Greater Seswenna territory fell under the Praesitlyn theatre. Deployed from Eriadu, Tarkin and his troops broke out from the salient and besieged the Separatists worlds of [[Triton/Legends|Triton]], [[Sluis Van/Legends|Sluis Van]] and [[Xagobah/Legends|Xagobah]].<ref name="Warfare" /> During the [[Battle of Xagobah (Clone Wars)|Battle of Xagobah]], Anakin Skywalker&mdash;by then a leading Jedi Knight whom Tarkin found to be a trustworthy ally&mdash;captured [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]. Fett insisted that he had information vital to the Republic's war effort, and demanded to see Chancellor Palpatine. Skywalker, not trusting Fett, sent him to Coruscant with instructions to turn himself over to the custody of Tarkin, whom Skywalker trusted to handle the matter. Tarkin traveled to the galactic capital and met Fett at the Jedi Temple. Tarkin left Fett in visitors' quarters while he attended to business with members of the Senate, but Fett sneaked out and attempted to kill Jedi Master Mace Windu, who had killed Fett's father [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]]. Palpatine covered up the incident after buying Fett's silence regarding the information the bounty hunter carried, which could have exposed Palpatine's secret scheme to orchestrate the Clone Wars to his own ends.<ref name="Pursuit" />

===Imperial potentate===
In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the Clone Wars ended with the defeat of the Separatists. Palpatine declared the Jedi enemies of the Republic, accusing them of [[Treason/Legends|treason]], and initiated a [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|purge]] of the Order. He also issued the [[Declaration of a New Order]], converting the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], with himself as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|emperor]].<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" /> The plans for Sienar's battle station, developed with a [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] capable of destroying planets, were put into effect with the long-delayed construction of what became known as the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]]&mdash;though Tarkin himself did not care for the name, regarding it as overly melodramatic.<ref name="Death Star" /> Tarkin, having thought the project dead, was shocked to learn that Palpatine had secretly followed through on the plans Tarkin had presented him a decade before, even beginning construction over Republic-occupied Geonosis without Tarkin's knowledge, and was frustrated that he had been left out of the development process.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /><ref name="Death Star" />

[[File:Moff_Tarkin.png|thumb|right|200px|Tarkin shows the Death Star, under construction, to Emperor Palpatine and Darth Vader.]]
Tarkin, who as Moff had been granted a special purview over the development of military technology, was entrusted with control over aspects of construction of the Death Star&mdash;and he hoped to gain total oversight of the project.<ref name="Dark Lord" /><ref name="Republic HoloNet News" /> Palpatine and his new [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]], Darth Vader, visited Tarkin early on to observe the construction of the Death Star.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" /> The Death Star's construction soon fell behind schedule, plagued by labor shortages, supply problems, failures on the part of contractors, and engineering dilemmas.<ref name="Dark Lord" /> The superlaser, the major technological innovation of the project, was not fully worked out, and the [[Hammertong/Legends|Hammertong Project]] continued research on the design.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> Repeated attempts at sabotage set back the problem, and intelligence leaks caused Tarkin to move the station's location completely, with [[Seswenna/Legends|Seswenna]] and the [[Patriim system/Legends|Patriim system]] among the early locations, delaying the massive project's progress.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /><ref name="The Essential Atlas" />

Palpatine soon arranged for Tarkin to meet with Vader to coordinate a response to the arrival of several fugitive Jedi, whom Tarkin had been monitoring, on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]]. Tarkin proposed that, rather than simply hunting down the Jedi, Vader implement a larger plan to [[Battle of Kashyyyk (19 BBY)|invade]] Kashyyyk on the justification that it was harboring Jedi and enslave many native [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]] for use as labor on the Death Star project. Tarkin hoped that the use of the strong and technologically skilled Wookiees would allow the project to return to pace. Vader did so, and Tarkin covertly moved the new slaves to the construction site. He reported on his cooperation with Vader to Palpatine, explaining that Imperial officers were unsure of the mysterious [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]]. Tarkin, however, was pleased with Vader, and asked permission to continue partnering with the Sith Lord.<ref name="Dark Lord" /> Tarkin was one of few Imperial officers to see potential in cooperating with Vader, and worked closely with the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] in the course of his career.<ref name="The Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Over time, Tarkin investigated Vader's origins, and found that the powerful Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker had been reported dead on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]], with no body produced, around the same time that Vader emerged in his life-support suit. Though he was not certain, Tarkin thought it likely that the two were one.<ref name="Death Star" />

As the Empire established itself, Tarkin was a driving intellectual force behind the new regime, second only to Palpatine in giving shape and vision to the Galactic Empire.<ref name="The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide" /> He offered scholarly arguments that supported the philosophies Palpatine articulated in rousing speeches, and early in the Empire's day, Tarkin authored the key work ''[[Visions of the New Order]]'', which quickly became a foundational text for the [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|Commission for the Preservation of the New Order]] and its agencies.<ref name="Rebellion Era Sourcebook" /> Tarkin was also a key Imperial military leader, known for the brutal tactics he used to gain his victories.<ref name="Official Starships & Vehicles 9" /> Moff Tarkin was among the highest-ranking personnel within the Empire, enjoying a rare exemption from security checks.<ref name="Against the Empire">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Against the Empire]]''</ref> Within a month after the war's end, Tarkin was granted the first of the powerful new [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperator''-class Star Destroyers]], [[Executrix/Legends|''Executrix'']], as his flagship.<ref name="Dark Lord" />

During his tenure as Moff, Admiral [[Garoche Tarkin]], an officer under Tarkin's charge and his son, went missing, believed to have vanished during a mission in the [[Atoan system]]. Seeking the Emperor's aid, Tarkin was appointed Vader for assistance, which he met with distaste, believing Vader's priorities to be petty and insufficient for the Empire's needs. Nonetheless, Tarkin followed the Emperor's command, and, as insurance, sent Captain [[Shale (human)|Shale]] with Vader to ensure the [[Atoan insurgency|mission's]] success.<ref name="DVLC1" /> As the mission came to a head, Shale gave a grim reminder to Vader that, if it ended in failure, Vader's command would come to an end at Tarkin's hands. The mission's success was vital to the Emperor as well; though he saw Garoche Tarkin as easily replaceable, he valued Tarkin's skills, and had no desire to allow the Moff to be distracted. However, Vader suggested that the death of his son could render Moff Tarkin more powerful; fueled by revenge, Tarkin could become a machine of destruction against the [[Atoan]] insurgents. Pondering Vader's plan, the Emperor approved, and ordered him to carry on.<ref name="DVLC2">[[Darth Vader and the Lost Command 2|''Darth Vader and the Lost Command'' 2]]</ref> The mission to the Atoan system was turned around when Shale betrayed Vader, realizing the Sith Lord's intent to murder Tarkin's son. Garoche himself was in fact disillusioned with his father's will, realizing that he had killed innocents in his name.<ref name="DVLC4">[[Darth Vader and the Lost Command 4|''Darth Vader and the Lost Command'' 4]]</ref> Garoche, Shale, and the remnants of the insurgency were themselves killed when Vader caused a cave-in on top of them; Garoche's death enraged Tarkin, causing him to grow thirsty for revenge and, in the Emperor's eyes, rendering him much more powerful, just as the Sith Lords had conspired.<ref name="DVLC5">[[Darth Vader and the Lost Command 5|''Darth Vader and the Lost Command'' 5]]</ref>

During his tenure as Moff, Tarkin came across a report that a probe had found an isolated stable pocket within [[Maw Cluster/Legends|the Maw]] black hole cluster. Suspecting that a secret safe spot within the notoriously dangerous cluster would prove a valuable asset, Tarkin erased the report before the data was passed beyond his desk. He then sent a surveying team that found other routes into the zone and confirmed that a base could be safely built within, then had the team killed to keep the area secret. Tarkin began considering uses for the location, but did not come up with any immediately.<ref name="The Jedi Academy Sourcebook">''[[The Jedi Academy Sourcebook]]''</ref> He made another acquisition when, at a fueling station on [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]] which Tarkin was in the process of expanding into a major refueling depot for the Imperial Navy, he met [[Tol Sivron]], an outcast former [[Head clan (Ryloth)|Head Clan]] member.<ref name="Champions of the Force">''[[Champions of the Force]]''</ref><ref name="The Essential Guide to Characters">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Tarkin took Sivron into his service and found the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] a competent manager.<ref name="Champions of the Force" />

[[File:Wilhuff_Tarkin-DSOTM.png|thumb|left|250px|Wilhuff Tarkin, the man behind the Ghorman Massacre]]
Early in Tarkin's Imperial career, high taxes on [[Ghorman/Legends|Ghorman]] prompted a sit-in protest at the spaceport. Tarkin, sent to collect the taxes from the defiant population, refused to yield, and landed his ship atop the peaceful protesters. Dozens were killed and hundreds injured in Tarkin's display of the consequences for defying the Imperial government. Despite public outrage at the [[Ghorman Massacre/Legends|Ghorman Massacre]]&mdash;which convinced Senator [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] to join Senator [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] in covertly plotting rebellion against the Empire&mdash;Palpatine declined to issue Tarkin any punishment; instead, he was soon promoted.<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Months after the Empire was declared, Tarkin met with Palpatine and [[Ferus Olin]], a former Jedi Padawan and anti-Imperial resistance fighter to whom Palpatine had offered amnesty if he would meet with the Emperor. Tarkin explained to Olin that the data systems of [[Samaria/Legends|Samaria]] had become corrupted and were disrupting services and identification systems. Palpatine requested that Olin, a computer expert, resolve the problem. After Palpatine threatened to have his partner, [[Roan Lands]], executed, Olin accepted the task, the first step of Palpatine's plan to corrupt Olin.<ref name="A Tangled Web">''[[The Last of the Jedi: A Tangled Web]]''</ref>

Having joined the Empire, Olin became a propaganda figure on his adopted homeworld of [[Bellassa/Legends|Bellassa]], where Tarkin and Vader initiated the [[Bellassan Project]]. They gathered a group of scientists&mdash;uncooperatives ones were forced to participate by the kidnapping of their families&mdash;to work on engineering problems related to the Death Star project, and hoped to use Bellassa's factories to manufacture components.<ref name="Secret Weapon">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Secret Weapon]]''</ref>

===Grand Moff Tarkin===
{{Quote|Rule through the fear of force rather than force itself.|Wilhuff Tarkin, in the Tarkin Doctrine|<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
In an [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]] personal communique to the Emperor, Tarkin proposed means to ensure Imperial security as a culmination of military and political theories he had long been developing.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /><ref name="Against the Empire" /><ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" /> Frustrated by cross-sector criminal and rebellious activity and the problem of jurisdictional conflicts, he called for the retooling of the oversector concept, proposing that oversectors be tailored to control unstable galactic hotspots and be assigned greater forces than usual in an attempt to root out rebellious activity before it could take hold.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> Each oversector, capable of crossing sector boundaries, would be controlled by a single official who answered directly to Palpatine. The installation of HoloNet transceivers aboard all flagships within an oversector would provide enhanced communication. The philosophy of power with which Tarkin suggested unrest be fought was that of rule through fear of force, rather than direct exercise of force. Displays of power, most vitally through the use of terror-inspiring superweapons, would, Tarkin suggested, stifle dissent and rebellion. The presentation of a seemingly invincible weapon of ultimate power would play upon the fearfulness and awe of the citizenry to render all thought of assault against the Empire forgotten.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" /> It was therefore Tarkin's recommendation that the Empire invest strongly and continually in the innovation of ever more powerful weapons of warfare.<ref name="Force Commander">''[[Star Wars: Force Commander]]''</ref> According to this philosophy, once the Death Star was active, no one would dare act against the Empire. Terror at the prospect of planetary annihilation would ensure compliance and order.<ref name="Death Star" /> Palpatine chose to officially recognize Tarkin's proposal, which became known as the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]], and Tarkin's theory became a central tenet of Imperial policy.<ref name="Death Star" /><ref name="Force Commander" />

[[File:Grand_Moff_Tarkin_2015_World_Championship_Prize.png|thumb|right|180px|Grand Moff Tarkin]]
The Tarkin Doctrine so pleased Palpatine that he immediately had his close aide, [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|Imperial Advisor]] [[Ars Dangor/Legends|Ars Dangor]] issue a response in his name conveying the Emperor's embrace of the Tarkin Doctrine and promotion of Tarkin to the rank of [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]], the position created for the officials in charge of oversectors.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" /><ref name="Death Star Technical Companion">''[[Death Star Technical Companion]]''</ref> Tarkin was the first man promoted to the new title.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Characters" /> He answered only to Palpatine and was given authority over [[Oversector Outer]], an expanded version of the Greater Seswenna sector that covered nearly the entire Outer Rim and some of the Mid Rim&mdash;the largest territory of any Imperial governor&mdash;and total control of the Death Star project.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /><ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /><ref name="The Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Death Star Technical Companion" /> [[Outer Rim Imperial Fleet|Pacifying]] the unruly Outer Rim Territories was considered among the most difficult assignments available in the Empire, but Tarkin was determined to tame the entire galaxy.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" />

Despite his vast responsibilties, Tarkin still found time for his personal life. Looking to advance his position, Tarkin sought out a wife. In [[10 BBY/Legends|10 BBY]] he married [[Thalassa Tarkin|Thalassa Motti]], of the influential [[Motti family]] of [[Phelarion/Legends|Phelarion]], for her contacts and money.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> Tarkin had no love for his wife, who remained on Phelarion overseeing her family's [[Megonite moss/Legends|megonite moss]] mines, but the Lady Tarkin was devoted to him.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="The Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Princess Leia Imperial Servant" /> At one point, a re-emergent Nebula Front faction on Eriadu kidnapped [[Shella Motti]], Tarkin's niece by marriage. Furious, Tarkin hired a group to rescue her. The situation was complicated when Motti refused to return, even hiring a bounty hunter of her own to counter Tarkin's agents.<ref name="Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds" />

Around the time of his marriage, Tarkin learned of a promising tactician, whose advances had revolutionized Imperial doctrines, performing exceptionally under a pseudonym on the Caridan Imperial networks.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> Tarkin began investigating, spending months and requiring the services of two underground [[Slicer/Legends|slicers]] to uncover the mystery tactician's identity. He discovered that this seeming genius was in fact [[Natasi Daala]], a Carida graduate serving as a kitchen corporal. He journeyed to [[Carida/Legends|Carida]] to meet her, and found that Daala was sure she had been shunted aside because of her sex. Seeing in her a potentially great officer, and concerned that the Caridan administration intended to transfer her to meteorological station to further hide their embarrassment at overlooking her talent, rather than promote her, Tarkin assigned her to his personal staff.<ref name="Darksaber">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']]</ref>

[[File:TarkinDorman.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Tarkin and Daala]]
Smitten with Daala, he began an affair, finding with her the passion that his marriage to Thalassa Tarkin lacked.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Jedi Search" /> In addition to being Tarkin's mistress, Daala was also his protégée; he tutored her in tactics and strategy and guided her ascent through the ranks.<ref name="Death Star" /><ref name="Jedi Search" /><ref name="Dark Apprentice">[[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']]</ref> Tarkin's relationship with Daala led to some rumors among subordinates that she had only obtained her rank by sleeping with the Grand Moff. Enraged when he overhead one young officer mutter a complaint to that effect, Tarkin had the lieutenant ejected in a spacesuit with a day's supply of air and piped his open comm over the intercom of his flagship so the entire crew were forced to listen as he raged, pleaded, and died. After that incident, Tarkin heard no further whispering.<ref name="Darksaber" />

Though he spent little time on Coruscant, Grand Moff Tarkin was a major figure in the Imperial Court. He was recognized as the definitive voice on policy and philosophy, second only to Palpatine.<ref name="Rebellion Era Sourcebook" /> At court, Tarkin had powerful allies, such as Darth Vader, [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Ruling Council]] member [[Janus Greejatus/Legends|Janus Greejatus]], and Imperial Advisor Lord [[Rodin Hlian Verpalion]], a close friend of Tarkin who admired the Grand Moff.<ref name="Death Star Technical Companion" /><ref name="Mission to Lianna">''[[Mission to Lianna]]''</ref><ref name="Janus Greejatus">{{DB|character|janusgreejatus|Greejatus, Janus}}</ref> In addition, Tarkin cultivated a cadre of ambitious subordinates, supporters, and clients, such as [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Merillion Tarko]], whom Tarkin had promoted to the rank of Moff; Moff [[Ariss Lyjan]] of the [[Nuiri sector/Legends|Nuiri sector]]; distant relative Admiral [[Sander Delvardus]], who commanded the Seswenna sector's fleet; and [[Commodore/Legends|Commodore]] Lord [[Tion (Lord)/Legends|Tion]].<ref name="Official Starships & Vehicles 9" /><ref name="The Essential Atlas" /><ref name="Wretched Hives of Scum & Villainy">''[[Wretched Hives of Scum & Villainy]]''</ref><ref name="The Essential Chronology">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref><ref name="The Force Unleashed II website">{{LucasArts|url=games/theforceunleashed2|text=''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II''}}</ref>

As one of the Empire's most powerful men, Tarkin was involved in a great deal of intrigue. To hide his secrets from political rivals, Tarkin routed many of his more sensitive matters through the [[Ubiqtorate/Legends|Ubiqtorate]] base on [[Yaga Minor/Legends|Yaga Minor]], over which he exercised a great deal of control. He implemented two access stations on an extended walkway to keep civilian researchers out of the rest of the base, keeping his own business more secure.<ref name="Vision of the Future">''[[Vision of the Future]]''</ref> To further protect himself, the Grand Moff kept spies within the commands of officers he mistrusted.<ref name="Heroes & Rogues">''[[Heroes & Rogues]]''</ref> It was not only his secrets Tarkin had to safeguard, but the Emperor's as well; Tarkin was among only a handful of high-ranking figures familiar with Palpatine's secret agents, the [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hands]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to the Force">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

[[File:Tarkin_SWSB.png|thumb|right|200px|Grand Moff Tarkin]]
In [[6 BBY/Legends|6 BBY]], Tarkin was part of the graduation ceremony at the [[Carida Academy/Legends|Academy of Carida]], in which he congratulated valedictorian [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and salutatorian [[Soontir Fel/Legends|Soontir Fel]]. Fel's response&mdash;that the honor of his class rank paled in comparison with the honor of serving the Empire&mdash;impressed Tarkin, and the Grand Moff made a point to watch Fel's career.<ref name="The Making of Baron Fel">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 25|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 25]]</ref> In the same year, Tarkin paid a visit to Viceroy Bail Prestor Organa of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], a man suspected of disloyalty to the Emperor, where he found himself struck by a water balloon dropped by Organa's daughter, [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]].<ref name="Official Starships & Vehicles 29">[[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 29|''Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection'' 29]]</ref>

Tarkin's exploits were not all political; he carried out the [[Atravis Sector Massacres]], and in [[5 BBY/Legends|5 BBY]], Tarkin commanded the subjugation of defiant [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Darksaber" /><ref name="Children of the Jedi">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref> The prominent [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] leader [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]] was enslaved and entered into the service of Tarkin's subordinate [[Unidentified Imperial fleet officer|naval officer]] commanding the conquest. To please Tarkin, however, the officer gave Ackbar to the Grand Moff as a servant.<ref name="Heir to the Empire Sourcebook">''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> Ackbar served as a personal aide and as a chauffeur, piloting Tarkin's shuttles.<ref name="Darksaber" /> Tarkin came to have a vague fondness for the reliable servant, considering him like a pet.<ref name="Death Star Technical Companion" /> He would often hold forth on his tactics to Ackbar in self-satisfaction, gloating about his plans to subjugate yet more worlds.<ref name="Dark Apprentice" />

When, in 5 BBY, Gideon Tarkin died in the [[Erhynradd Mutiny]], Wilhuff Tarkin took Gideon's daughter, [[Rivoche Tarkin|Rivoche]], into his home.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> As a girl in her early teens, with her family dead, Rivoche expressed her grief in frequent tantrums. Never a warm family man at the best of times, Tarkin disciplined his niece by sending a friendly serving girl and her family to a penal asteroid. Rivoche quickly learned to behave for her uncle, who soon sent her to an elite preparatory academy on [[Clær]], where she learned to fill her role as an elite socialite.<ref name="Cracken's Rebel Operatives" />

===Building the Death Star===
{{Quote|The average citizen deals in symbols, not rational analysis. If we present the citizen with a weapon so powerful, so immense as to defy all conceivable attack against it, a weapon invulnerable and invincible in battle, that shall become the symbol for the Empire. We may need only a handful, perhaps only one of these weapons to subjugate thousands upon thousands of worlds containing millions upon millions of beings.|Wilhuff Tarkin, in a communique to Palpatine|<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" />}}
Construction of the Death Star, meanwhile, had been delayed interminably by sabotage, accidents, political maneuvering, administrative roadblocks, disputes with unions, and, most importantly, problems with the plans.<ref name="Death Star" /> After several years, critics began to doubt the central concept the station, the superlaser, believing it would not function. Tarkin privately worried that they might be correct.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> In any case, it was clear that the Death Star plans contained numerous flaws.<ref name="Death Star" />

Tarkin decided that the best remedy would be to create a prototype as a proof of concept.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> In [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]], Tarkin created the [[Maw Installation]] to solve the problems in the design, complete the Hammertong Project's work by proving the superlaser, create a model Death Star, and engineer yet more superweapons.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /><ref name="The Essential Atlas" /><ref name="Death Star" /> The Grand Moff had several asteroids moved into the hidden stable zone he had found within the Maw and built a hidden scientific facility into the interlinked asteroids; the workers were then killed to keep the think tank secret.<ref name="Jedi Search" /> He brought together a wealth of elite engineers, including head designer Bevel Lemelisk, [[Ohran Keldor]], and [[Umak Leth]] to contribute to the design, all of whom he personally vetted.<ref name="Death Star" /> Necessary scientists who did not volunteer were kidnapped.<ref name="The Essential Chronology" /> Tarkin appointed Tol Sivron the director of the facility, having been impressed with the alien's managerial skills, and hired the [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] lawyer and administrator [[Yemm]], whom he had met and found suitable at an Eriadu function, for an administrative position.<ref name="The Jedi Academy Sourcebook" /><ref name="Champions of the Force" /> Tarkin altered the records of military personnel assigned to the base to list them as dead, keeping their presence secret.<ref name="The Essential Chronology" />

[[File:TarkinLemelisk.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Tarkin and Lemelisk review the Death Star's design.]]
In order to maintain strict secrecy and to hide his mistress, he assigned Daala to guard the facility, with orders to remain at her post and capture or destroy any stray ships that came across the well-hidden facility.<ref name="Death Star" /><ref name="Jedi Search" /> He promoted her to admiral and presented her with four ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers as her fleet, personally taking her in a shuttle to observe them while under construction and impart to her the magnitude of power he was granting her.<ref name="The Jedi Academy Sourcebook" /><ref name="Jedi Search" /> Communication with the station was only possible through a communications circuit Tarkin controlled; the Emperor was the only other being to know of the Maw Installation's existence.<ref name="Death Star" />

Finally in a position to exploit the Omwati, he forced the planet's children to take an abilities test and collected hundreds of the highest-scoring children.<ref name="Alien Anthology" /> The primary program took ten ten-year-old children from Omwat and forced them through an advanced education program, for which Tarkin recruited noted experts [[Nasdra Magrody]] and Ohran Keldor as professors, hoping to form genius engineers.<ref name="Jedi Search" /><ref name="Children of the Jedi" /> The children labored for two years in an [[orbital education sphere]] over Omwat; those that suffered breakdowns from the tremendous pressure and pace of the accelerated program, or simply failed an examination, watched as their home cities were destroyed by orbital bombardment.<ref name="Jedi Search" /><ref name="Dark Apprentice" /> [[Qwi Xux]] was the only one to make it through the process, and Tarkin placed her at the Maw Installation under Lemelisk.<ref name="Jedi Search" />

Tarkin quite enjoyed Lemelisk's enthusiasm for the project, and was greatly pleased with his technological innovations. Tarkin demanded that Lemelisk's team integrate heavy defenses, comparable to those of a Core planet, into the design, and also that they ensure the station would be self-sufficient. Tarkin was disappointed that Lemelisk was not able to include much shielding in the design, but his demands were otherwise met.<ref name="Death Star Technical Companion" /> The engineers produced an amended set of plans that solved the problems detected in the earlier specifications, and Tarkin and Lemelisk presented the revised designs to Palpatine, who was elated that the Death Star's potential was soon to be reached and approved construction of a prototype.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /><ref name="Darksaber" /> The design team was able to build the desired [[Death Star prototype]] as a proof of the superlaser concept, and used it to further refine the design into a form ready for renewed construction efforts.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /><ref name="Death Star" /> Tarkin was delighted by the functional prototype, issuing Lemelisk, Xux, and Sivron medals immediately upon seeing their work.<ref name="Champions of the Force" />

After nearly two decades, the Death Star was little more than an incomplete framework. With the prototype having worked out most problems with the design, Tarkin restarted work on the Death Star with new energy.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /><ref name="Death Star" /> He removed Lemelisk from the Maw Installation, bringing him to oversee construction in the field.<ref name="Jedi Search" /> Tarkin charged the remaining scientists to create yet more powerful and devastating superweapons, such as the [[World Devastator]] and [[Sun Crusher]] projects, and insisted that they be ready within nine years.<ref name="Death Star" /><ref name="Jedi Search" /> After moving the Death Star from site to site in attempts to avoid sabotage by rebels against the Empire, the station's framework was finally emplaced over the Empire's most secure prison planet, [[Despayre]], in the [[Horuz system/Legends|Horuz system]].<ref name="Death Star" /> The planet's convicts were conscripted into the labor force&mdash;harshly overseen by Major [[Calders]] to Tarkin's great approval&mdash;and Tarkin assembled the largest force of construction droids in history to work toward the massive station's completion.<ref name="Death Star" /><ref name="Death Star Technical Companion" /> The Horuz system was heavily exploited for its natural resources, and fabrication systems and laboratories were erected in orbit to forge building materials and produce technical components. The entire project was carried out in strict secrecy, with a strong security detail in case the system and a shield generator on Despayre that projected a protective field over the Death Star's frame.<ref name="Death Star" /> An entire branch of the Imperial Navy, [[Battle Station Operations/Legends|Battle Station Operations]], was created to man the station. Tarkin had a [[Death Star Trooper/Legends|corps of elite soldiers]] created for station security, who received advanced training and were trained for intense loyalty.<ref name="Death Star Technical Companion" />

[[File:TarkinDeathStar.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Tarkin spent much of his time overseeing the construction of the Death Star.]]
Tarkin relied upon four major aides and advisors in constructing and running the station: Admiral [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]], General [[Cassio Tagge/Legends|Cassio Tagge]], General [[Moradmin Bast/Legends|Moradmin Bast]], and Major [[Siward Cass/Legends|Siward Cass]].<ref name="Death Star" /> Motti, a relative of Tarkin's wife, was his chief aide, and commanded the forces guarding the project; Tarkin believed him an overrated officer.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Death Star Technical Companion" /> He had far more respect for the abilities of Tagge, the other of his two joint seconds in command, who was charged with operational security and was to be responsible for the day-to-day running of the station itself once the Death Star was operational.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /><ref name="Death Star Technical Companion" /> Tagge's conservative belief that the Imperial Senate was necessary for the smooth running of the Empire diminished Tarkin's regard for him, however, and Tagge in turn thought little of Tarkin.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Death Star Technical Companion" /> Motti and Tagge's constant feuding over military doctrine and political position frustrated Tarkin, who wanted the station to run smoothly.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /><ref name="Death Star" /> Bast was Tarkin's primary personal aide, while Cass, an career aide of Tarkin for many years, served as a secondary personal aide and the chief communications officer on the battle station. <ref name="Chief Bast">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Chief Bast}}</ref> Other officers were vital to Tarkin's ability to run the station as well, such as Colonel [[Wullf Yularen/Legends|Wullf Yularen]], the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] officer responsible for briefing the Grand Moff.<ref name="Colonel Wullf Yularen">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Colonel Wullf Yularen}}</ref>

When Lemelisk expressed dissatisfaction with the work of untrained Despayre inmates, whose shoddy work was leading to mistakes and delaying construction, Tarkin responded by executing the current workforce and bringing in strong and technically proficient Wookiee slaves.<ref name="Darksaber" /> In 3 BBY, Tarkin presided over another invasion of Kashyyyk, leading his forces onto the planet personally and demanding that Wookiee leaders provide workers.<ref name="Darksaber" /><ref name="Pax Empirica">{{StoryCite|story=Pax Empirica&mdash;The Wookiee Annihilation|book=Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Prima's Official Strategy Guide}}</ref> When they refused, Tarkin's forces fired on the planet, rounded up Wookiees, and executed any who resisted. Tarkin kept some hostages in camps on Kashyyyk, using them to threaten the construction workers into compliance, along with drugs and [[negative-stimulation transmitter]]s.<ref name="Darksaber" />

Due to further delays, Darth Vader visited the under-construction Death Star for the first time, met by Tarkin and Lemelisk. Lemelisk, to Tarkin's annoyance, complained to Vader of obstruction by the Wookiee slaves, Vader reviewed the records of construction foremen and had Tarkin call a meeting of crew supervisors. In front of the others, Vader executed the two least efficient foremen and had their bodies mounted on the Death Star's framework. Tarkin was pleased to see that future construction work sped up.<ref name="Darksaber" />
